description:
Find packaging: the titles and thumbnails that earned the click on a topic, from
    long-form YouTube videos that beat their own channel.

    What it does: runs the same outlier search as find_long_hooks (long-form YouTube,
    2023 or later, views at least min_outlier times the channel's usual), then looks at
    each video's thumbnail beside its title and says what the pair is doing.

    What comes back: the run's `finds`, ranked. Each is a real package, as YouTube shows
    it: title (verbatim) and thumbnail_url (the size YouTube really served, the picture
    the analysis looked at; thumbnail_checked says so), channel, watch_url, views,
    channel_median_views, outlier, outlier_score (0 to 100 on one fixed scale, so finds
    from different runs rank together), outlier_tier, channel_size and posted_at, plus the analysis: title_device (curiosity_gap, contrarian_claim,
    specific_number, how_to, listicle, challenge, story, question, warning, comparison,
    authority, timeliness, identity_callout, other), title_template (the title as a
    fill-in structure), thumbnail_text (the words printed on the thumbnail, read by a vision
    model; null when none), thumbnail_text_role (repeats_title, adds_to_title,
    contrasts_title, no_text), thumbnail_subject, thumbnail_faces, thumbnail_emotion,
    thumbnail_colors, thumbnail_composition, thumbnail_devices, angle, gap (what the picture shows that the title does not say, and the
    question that leaves), promise, steal_it and audience. analysed is false when a package
    could not be looked at; it is still a real package.

    The run's report then holds title_patterns and thumbnail_patterns (what at least two
    of the packages share, each naming their video_ids) and ideas: up to `ideas` (6 by
    default, 0 for none) packages WRITTEN for your topic from those patterns, each a title
    a thumbnail concept and thumbnail_text (the words to print on it), naming the real
    packages it is based_on. report.ideas_label is always "Written by Hook Detector from
    the patterns in these real packages": show it with them, never present an idea as a
    real video's title. report.numbers counts the packages: title_chars and title_words
    (medians), titles_with_number, titles_with_question, thumbnails_with_text and
    thumbnail_words (over the analysed ones), and the title_devices, thumbnail_devices and
    emotions that repeat (name, count). report.landscape is the subject at a glance, as on
    find_long_hooks.

    Arguments: topic 3 to 500 characters, or a channel's or a long-form video's YouTube
    address exactly as on find_long_hooks (a channel's own outliers, or that one video; no
    ideas are written for a link, use remix_find); count 1 to 24 (default 12); language,
    country, min_outlier, posted_within_days, channel_size and reuse as on
    find_long_hooks; idempotency_key and wait_seconds as on find_hooks.

    Cost: reserves up to 70 credits (down to 25) and charges only the provider calls it
    made: the searches, one call per channel measured, and one for each video whose date
    had to be read exactly. Looking at a thumbnail costs no credit. After a find_long_hooks run on the same topic it is close
    to free. A failed run costs nothing, and so does a run that finds nothing, inside the
    allowance.

    Timing and next step: how long a run takes has not been measured yet, so never assume
    a time. Call get_run with wait_seconds=50 until status is done or failed. Same as
    POST /v1/packaging. Needs the research permission.

channel_size.description: optional: only videos from channels of this size, by what the channel's uploads usually get (its median views, the figure the outlier is measured against): small (under 20,000), medium (up to 200,000) or large. Null or left out: any size
channel_size.title: Channel Size

count.description: how many packages to deliver, 1 to 24
count.title: Count

country.description: optional, an assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (US, GB, MA): searches YouTube as seen from this country. It steers the search; it does not filter the channels
country.title: Country

ideas.description: optional, 0 to 10 (default 6): how many written packages (a title and a thumbnail concept) to add for the subject; 0 for none
ideas.title: Ideas

idempotency_key.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters; the same key within 24 hours returns the first run instead of paying for a second
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

language.description: optional, up to 60 characters: the language the videos should be spoken in, in words or as a tag ("Spanish", "pt-BR"). Left out, it is read from the topic's own language
language.title: Language

min_outlier.description: optional, 1.5 to 100 (default 2): how many times its own channel's usual views a video must have to count as an outlier. Only outliers are ever delivered
min_outlier.title: Min Outlier

posted_within_days.description: optional, how recent the videos must be, as days: 30, 90, 365, 730. Null or left out means everything since 2023-01-01; nothing older is ever delivered
posted_within_days.title: Posted Within Days

reuse.description: start from the videos your last long or packaging run on this topic already bought (within a week), so the second tab on a topic costs little
reuse.title: Reuse

topic.description: the subject to research, 3 to 500 characters, in any language. Or a YouTube address instead of a subject: a channel's (https://www.youtube.com/@name, or just @name) returns that channel's own outliers, its recent long-form uploads that beat its usual; a long-form video's (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...) returns that one video, whatever its multiple. A Short's address is refused (422)
topic.title: Topic

wait_seconds.description: 0 to 50: seconds to wait for the run to finish; 0 returns at once
wait_seconds.title: Wait Seconds

name: find_packaging
